thread.title: Apple’s stock just broke out from a 2-month hibernation - MarketWatch

author: Barbara Kollmeyer
title: Apple’s stock just broke out from a 2-month hibernation - MarketWatch
text:
Look alive out there this morning, because it’s looking like a big day for stocks.
The Dow has busted out to a new record near 26,000 as traders come back from the Martin Luther King Jr. holiday, seemingly eager to dive back into this rally. It’s the opposite for bitcoin and cryptocurrencies, which may be in the throes of a “Black Monday”-style selloff:
It is getting worse. Crypto is now worse than Black Monday, the worst single day in stock market history. pic.twitter.com/7WqH4QubPA
— John_Hempton (@John_Hempton) January 16, 2018 We’re kicking off with the chart of the day , which is timely as several tech stocks like Netflix NFLX, +0.14% and Amazon AMZN, -0.03% are making headway this morning. The subject of that chart is one investor favorite — Apple AAPL, -0.51% , which broke out to a new all-time high on Friday of $177.09.
The chart comes from MKM Partners’ chief market technician, Jonathan Krinsky:
MKM Partners/Bloomberg Apple may have just ignited its chances of becoming the first trillion-dollar company, driven by a strong trend and momentum, points out Krinsky in a note to clients.
Krinsky notes that in Friday’s action, 33% of the S&P 500 components hit a 52-week high — the most in nearly five years. He warns this often means some kind of short-term pullback for stocks.
And that’s where Apple comes in. He says it’s one stock that still has potential to run higher, even given the strong leg-up equities have experienced so far this year.
Focus on “strong long-term trends that have been in near-term consolidations, and therefore are not short-term overbought,” Krinsky advises.
Among the other stocks that he says fit the bill: AECOM ACM, -0.54% , Disney DIS, -1.58% , MGM MGM, +2.85% , PPG PPG, -1.29% , Terex TEX, -0.43% and Ecolab ECL, -0.48%
Overall, investors should be on the lookout for some short-term consolidation for the S&P.
“A 5% decline would simply test the rising 50 [daily moving average], certainly not out of the question,” Krinsky says.

Key market gauges The Dow DJIA, -0.04% has opened at 26,000, with the S&P 500 SPX, -0.35% and Nasdaq COMP, -0.51% also well into the green. Asia stocks have come back from a Monday slide, while European stocks SXXP, +0.13% are moving up , with a weaker euro cutting the index a break.
Opinion: Only 1 stock-market sector has seen real earnings gains in the past 12 months
The dollar DXY, -0.02% sold off hard Monday, but has been bouncing back this morning. Gold GCH8, +0.32% is nearing its best level in four months , while oil prices CLH8, -0.78% are weaker.
Check out the Market Snapshot column for more.
Cryptocurrencies are in a world of pain, with bitcoin BTCUSD, -22.31% BTCUSD, -22.31% hitting a 6-week low below $12,000, as concerns over a South Korea crackdown persist .
The chart One reason to buy commodities? They’re cheap relative to stocks. That’s the message in our call of the day from Justin Brill, blogging for Daily Wealth over the weekend.
He notes that the Bloomberg Commodity Index is up 11% since bottoming in late June, with about half of those gains taking place over just the past four weeks.
“Commodities have only been this cheap relative to stocks two other times in the past 50 years. And in both cases, commodities dramatically outperformed stocks over the next several years,” says Brill.
The first time that happened was in the early ‘70s, just before the dollar had been taken off the gold standard, he notes. The second time was before the last melt-up for stocks during the dot-com boom.
“What many folks don’t realize is that many commodities actually bottomed more than a year before the stock market peaked. And again, they trounced the stock market for years,” adds Brill.
One way to play this comes from the blogger’s colleague Steve Sjuggerud, who recommends the iShares MSCI Global Metals & Mining Producers Fund PICK, -2.75% , of which Rio Tinto RIO, -3.28% and BHP Billiton BHP, -2.92% are top holdings.
The buzz GE GE, -2.93% is sinking after the company said it will take a $6.2 billion charge in the fourth quarter.
Merck MRK, +5.81% is jumping on news of positive results from a lung-cancer trial .
ETP ETP, +0.00% is up after USA Compression Partners USAC, +0.97% says it will buy the former’s compression business in a deal valued at about $1.8 billion .
Also in deal news, IBM IBM, +0.44% is up on a planned blockchain joint venture with global shipping giant Maersk MAERSKB, -0.53% . And Long Blackchain LBCC, -2.19% says it has entered into a letter of intent to merge with Stater Blockchain .
UnitedHealth UNH, +1.86% is up after posting a profit beat , while Citi C, +0.35% is also up, even though it lost $18.3 billion in the fourth quarter, owing to a tax charge . Goldman Sachs GS, +0.56% and Morgan Stanley MS, -0.94% are coming this week.

BP BP, -3.30% says it will take a $1.7 billion charge over the Deepwater Horizon disaster .

The Empire state factory gauge fell for a third month . Don’t forget that the countdown for the government shutdown is on. Here’s how stocks have handled that in the past .
The stat Getty Images A member of idol group Virtual Currency Girls and fan 80% — That’s how much bitcoin has been mined, reports The CoinTelegraph .
“This means only 4.2 million bitcoins, or 20%, are left to mine until bitcoin’s 21 million supply cap is reached,” it said.
For investors in the digital currency, scarcity is a good thing — even if it’s a bit rough out there today.
